title: bf16 Rounding Silently Discards Most RL Policy Updates: A Hidden Training-Inference Mismatch and an Unbiased One-Line Fix
date: 29 October 2026 (arXiv v1, the only version as of 2 November 2026)

code.title: andrewgcodes/faircast
code.note: The faircast package (sr_cast_bf16, ef_cast_bf16, the straight-through served-copy forward; torch only), a 60-line GRPO example on GSM8K, the Modal training harness with the 87 per-arm configurations, the 25 matched pairs behind Table 2 and the MBPP+ held-out curves (MIT; read at commit 7c213b2 of 29 October 2026). The per-step logs the figure scripts read are not in the repository

takeaway: On single-GPU GRPO runs with Qwen3-0.6B to 4B, exporting the fp32 master to the bf16 sampler with stochastic rounding and computing the loss on that served copy, instead of round-to-nearest, ended more than one point ahead in held-out accuracy on 18 of 25 matched seed-pairs, within one point on 6 and behind on 1 (mean +6.1 points, median +3.1, much of it from three zebra-puzzle pairs).
verdict: Believe the mechanism: the dead-zone arithmetic is exact, the fix is a few lines of released code, and the paper measures the lag directly (one optimizer step moves an fp32 sampler from 0.17 to 0.84 while the bf16 export stays at 0.19). Treat the size of the gain as provisional: one training implementation, models up to 4B, mostly single seeds, 14 of the 25 differences smaller than one standard error, a mean carried by three zebra pairs, and one task (list functions) where removing the lag cost 14.5 points until an explicit EMA lag was added back.
